To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
young women in Denmark have a poor knowledge of HPV and its role as a cause of cervical dyspalsia and cancer and of genital warta, and that they are not aware of the benefits of HPV vaccination.
young women's attitudes towards the HPV vaccine are mainly influenced by the perceived benefits of vaccination, the costs of the vaccine, and the availability of information about the vaccine.

the most important reasons for acceptance were the prevention of cervical cancer and the recommendation of healthcare professionals, whereas the most important barriers were the cost and a lack of knowledge about the benefits of HPV vaccination for sexually active young women.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the attitudes of young women to vaccination against HPV and their knowledge of HPV and cervical cancer.
the reasons why young women decide to accept or reject the HPV vaccination.
the reasons why women aged 16 to 26 accept or reject the HPV vaccine, the information available to them and the barriers and drivers to acceptance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the uptake of HPV vaccination is low and that the reasons for this are multifactorial and complex.
the uptake of HPV vaccination is low in Denmark and that this is mainly due to the high costs of vaccination.
the most important barriers for vaccination were cost and a lack of knowledge about the benefits of the vaccine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is a need for more information and knowledge about HPV and its consequences in the general public and that this should be targeted at the younger age groups in particular.
the main drivers to acceptance of HPV vaccination were: the prevention of cervical cancer; parental encouragement; and financial support.

the most important drivers for acceptance of the HPV-vaccine are the prevention of cervical cancer, parental encouragement and financial supports, personal experience of cancer and recommendation by the health-care professionals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Danish HPV vaccination campaign was insufficient and that the information given to young women was inadequate.
there is a clear need for more information about HPV and its consequences for sexually active women.
the cost of HPV vaccination is the most important factor for women's acceptance or refusal of the vaccine.
